title: SLO Conservator — Field Manual for Capacity Hedging and Error‑Budget Governance
author: Anika Patel
body:
Overview

This field manual describes the SLO Conservator concept: a combined human+automation operational pattern for proactively hedging capacity, protecting error budgets, and orchestrating tenant-level mitigations during multi-tenant inference surges. The Conservator is an SRE practice and a small orchestration service that acts as the authoritative executor for short-term capacity hedges and tenant-level graceful degradation.

Purpose and scope
- Provide a single operational playbook for when and how to: preemptively allocate runway, enact tenant throttles/evictions, shift traffic to fallbacks, and coordinate escalations.
- Cover both automatic Conservator behaviors and the runbook for on-call SREs to validate, override, and handoff.
- Apply to Redwood inference workloads across Hosted / Dedicated / Private serving modes where multi-tenant capacity contention can cause SLO risk.

When to use the Conservator
1) Consumption spike forecast where projected headroom < 2x expected 15-minute burst.
2) Error budget burn rate > 4x baseline for a service group for > 30 minutes.
3) Multi-model rollout producing unexplained tail-latency regressions.
4) Cross-region outage requiring redistribution of critical tenants.

Key concepts and terms
- Conservator: an authorized controller (automated + human-in-the-loop) that adjusts routing, throttles tokens, and triggers reserve capacity.
- Runway: short-term capacity margin measured in reservable GPU-pool seconds or token throughput for the next 30–60 minutes.
- Tenant Score: composite health score per tenant (latency quantile, error-rate delta, reserved commit).
- Evacuation window: safe time budget for draining a model/tenant from a node before preemption.

Ownership and roles
- Conservator Owner: eng-sre (primary), contacts: oncall@redwood.com, page SRE rotation lead.
- Automation Owner: eng-platform (maintains conservator service).
- Escalation: if automated mitigation fails within 10 minutes, escalate to Service Owner(s) listed on the tenant manifest.

SLA / SLO alignment
- Conservator actions must target prevention of SLO breach for high-priority tenants (SLO class P1/P2).
- Conservator policy thresholds are conservative — aim to keep per-service p99 latency within 10% of baseline.

Operational properties and safety
- Conservator must be idempotent and rate-limited: max 1 throttle/change per tenant per 60 seconds by default.
- Every automated action should produce: audit event, evidence (metric snapshot), and rollback token.
- Human overrides attach a reason and expire automatically after the safe window.

Activation runbook: Guided procedure for oncall SRE
1) Triage & verification
   a) Confirm alert provenance (Prometheus alert ID / Conservator telemetry).
   b) Pull metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error-rate, headroom. Example PromQL: 
      sum(rate(inference_requests_total[1m])) by (tenant) / sum(node_token_capacity)
   c) Check Correlation: recent deploys, model changes, quantization toggles.
2) Decide Conservator mode
   - Auto (automation allowed): if burn-rate > 5x and runway < 45m AND no active planned rollout.
   - Manual (SRE must confirm): if tenant-affecting evictions will touch enterprise tenants.
3) Execute Conservative Mitigations (stepwise)
   1. Increase batching target by +10% for non-P1 tenants (if runtime supports dynamic batching).
   2. Enable prefix-KV cache prioritization for warm tenants.
   3. Apply per-tenant soft-throttle: 10% token admission reduction for lowest Tenant Score.
   4. If no improvement in 5 minutes, escalate to hard throttle (50%) or move tenant to standby variant model.
4) Reserve capacity and re-route
   - If Dedicated pool has burst capacity, trigger reserve allocation API: 
     curl -X POST https://platform.internal/reserve-capacity 
       -d '{"pool":"dedicated-a","seconds":1800,"priority":"conservator"}' 
   - Re-route non-critical tenant traffic to backup region or quantized model variant with documented quality regression.
5) Announce and document
   - Post a short event on the incident channel: who, why, actions, expected rollback time.
   - Add audit note to ticketing system with rollback token and runbook step ids.

Automated Conservator policy: thresholds and actions (operator-facing)
| Signal | Threshold | Primary action | Max impact window |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Runway (minutes) | < 60 | engage soft-throttle & reserve capacity | 120 |
| Service error burn-rate (1h) | > 4x | reduce admission per low-score tenant 10% -> 50% | 30 |
| p99 latency delta | > +25% | move top offenders to quantized fallback | 20 |
| Node OOM risk score | > 0.7 | drain affected model warm-pool | 15 |

Note: thresholds are configurable per-cluster via Conservator policies stored in S3: s3://redwood-configs/conservator/policies/{cluster}.yaml

Conservator policy YAML excerpt (example)
-----
cluster: us-west-2
runway_threshold_minutes: 60
soft_throttle_steps: [10, 25, 50]
max_automated_evictions_per_hour: 2
protected_tenant_tags: ["enterprise", "sla-high"]
metric_sources:
  - prometheus: "https://prometheus.us-west-2"
-----

Observability and evidence collection
- Required telemetry snapshot for every action (persisted for 30 days):
  - topology snapshot (node count, GPU types)
  - tenant-level qps, latency quantiles, error-rates (5m/1h/24h)
  - recent deploys and model-variant changes
- Conservator exposes a /telemetry endpoint and emits events to Kafka topic conservator.events.

CLI quick commands (SRE operator)
- Dry-run a policy: 
  conservatorctl simulate --cluster=us-west-2 --policy=default --duration=15m
- Apply manual soft-throttle to tenant: 
  conservatorctl throttle --tenant=tenant-42 --percent=25 --reason="p99-latency-spike"
- Force rollback last action: 
  conservatorctl rollback --ticket=INC-12345 --token=abcde-rollback

Escalation matrix
1) Conservator automated mitigation fails to improve signals within 15 minutes: page Conservator oncall (PagerDuty SRE-Team-Conservator).
2) If Tenant is tagged enterprise or SLA-high and impact persists > 30 minutes: page Product/Account owner and Customer Success.
3) If multiple clusters show correlated runway collapse: trigger incident commander and follow Major Incident runbook.

Post-action checklist and postmortem requirements
- Every Conservator activation (automated or manual) must produce a ticket containing: 
  - timeline of actions with timestamps and rollback tokens,
  - metric snapshots pre/post action,
  - owner for follow-up remediation and RCA lead.
- If action included tenant eviction/hard throttle, produce a customer-facing summary approved by legal & CS before external comms.
- RCA expectations: complete timeline, causal factors, mitigation efficacy, long-term remediation plan, and policy changes; due within 7 business days.

Testing and rehearsal cadence
- Quarterly tabletop focused on: sudden model-tenant surge, rollout-triggered tail-latency, and cross-region loss.
- Engineering must include Conservator policies in CI for canary simulation tests.

Safety exceptions and policy change process
- To change a Conservator policy that affects protected_tenant_tags, require review by SRE manager + Product + Security.
- Emergency policy change allowed when: imminent SLO breach on P1 tenants; must be ratified in the next 48 hours.

Related pages and references
- Service onboarding: capacity-runway template (link internal)
- Conservator automation repo: git@internal:redwood/conservator.git
- Prometheus alert rules: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/alerting-index

Appendix: Example incident vignette (short)
- Scenario: small push created a quantization flag misconfiguration that doubled per-token time for a model subset. Conservator detected p99 +40% and runway dropping under 45m. Automated policy performed soft-throttles on least-critical tenants, reserved 1800s of burst capacity, and moved two non-enterprise tenants to quantized fallback. P99 recovered within 12 minutes; automation escalated a ticket for rollout rollback and model profiling.
